svg.text: The pregnant adolescent: a different risk profile, not a smaller adult
Higher obstetric risk
Pre-eclampsia and eclampsia
Obstructed labour — the pelvis may still be
growing, so cephalopelvic disproportion
Preterm birth and low birth weight
Anaemia, competing with her own growth
Obstetric fistula after prolonged labour
Plan the birth where a theatre is available.
What she also needs
A confidential consultation, at least partly
without her mother in the room
Screening for coercion and for violence
Support to return to school after the birth
Contraception before discharge, because a
second pregnancy within a year is common
Judgement in your face will end the consultation.
The safeguarding question you must ask yourself
In Ghana the age of consent to sexual intercourse is 16, and defilement of a child under 16 is a criminal offence
regardless of whether the child appeared to agree. A pregnant 13-year-old is evidence of a crime.
Marriage under 18 is prohibited under the Children's Act 1998, Act 560.
Your duty is to the child in front of you: treat her, document carefully, and follow the safeguarding pathway.
Consent to medical treatment is a separate question from consent to sex, and the age for treatment is 18.
How adolescent-friendly services differ in practice
Timing that does not clash with school · A separate space or a separate hour · No demand for a partner or parent
Staff who do not comment on her situation · Confidentiality explained out loud, with its limits stated honestly
She will judge the whole health service by the first thirty seconds of how you speak to her.
